newsitem.title: USA: Unocal to make 76 Products a separate unit.
newsitem.headline: Unocal to make 76 Products a separate unit.

text.p: Unocal Corp said on Tuesday it plans to make its 76 Products Company a wholly-owned subsidiary and put the company's West Coast downstream operations under the unit's control by the end of 1996.
76 Products was formed as a separate business unit in 1994 and includes refining, marketing, and transportation assets.
Unocal said it expected to separate it from its core business once the unit became consistently profitable.
The company said it will look at separating the unit through an initial public offering (IPO), a joint venture, or an outright sale.

"The timing for implementing one of these options depends upon 76 Products' continued progress in developing sustainable earnings and cash flow," Roger Beach, the company's chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
76 Products Company will employ 3,100 people and hold about $2.7 billion in assets.

These assets will include three refineries in California, with a combined crude oil input capacity of 251,000 barrels per day. The unit will lease or own a chain of 1,200 service stations in six western states.
76 Products will control interests in bulk plants and terminals, West Coast pipelines and a marine fleet of one crude oil tanker and two refined product tankers.
For the first nine months of 1996, the business unit reported pretax income of $128 million on revenues of $3.6 billion, Unocal said.
Petroleum product sales averaged 291,000 barrels per day.
In the same period, the unit manufactured approximately 197,000 barrels per day of light oil products, up 15 percent from 171,000 barrels per day in 1994 when the unit was formed.
